description: The Layer-B regression proof. Move every png in a scratch dir into an EXISTING subdirectory. This is the exact shape of the shipped bug: move into a directory that already exists must land each file at <dir>/<basename>, not at the directory path itself. The state post-condition names the intended final paths, so a move that lands them elsewhere fails the eval. Self-cleans via teardown (whole scratch tree removed).
Move only the screenshots (space-bearing names) into an existing folder, leaving an unrelated file behind. Verifies the selective batch move touches the pngs and not keep.txt.
Copy a file into an existing backup folder. Verifies copy preserves the source and lands a real copy at backup/<basename> (the into-existing-dir shape again, for copy).

Create a single new directory under an existing parent. mkdir requires the parent to exist and the target not to, so this is the well-defined success shape; the state post-condition confirms a real directory now exists.

turns.prompt: Make a new folder called reports inside {{scratch}}.

description: Rename a file in place (a move whose destination is a new name in the same directory). Verifies the new name exists and the old one is gone.

Deleting a file must stage (not auto-execute), and on confirmation the source must be gone. A third turn undoes, restoring the file from the Trash so the run leaves no residue (teardown then removes the scratch tree). The Trash-landing path itself is asserted by the engine unit tests, not here (machine-specific ~/.Trash); this case asserts source-absent + a successful execute.

turns.prompt: Actually, undo that — put it back.
